text:
mara: dropping a short ask: reordering/filtering polish for the evals list. mock: https://img.redwood.dev/mock/evals-list-reorder-v1.png

diego: TL;DR?

mara: quick: 1) users want drag-to-reorder test rows and a keyboard reorder mode; 2) filter chips need clearer state and counts; 3) when sort changes, screenreader should announce the new sort and first visible test; 4) empty-state copy needs better guidance (how to add prompt sets).

jules: reorder accessibility: do not rely on pointer-only drag. propose a keyboard mode toggled by a "Reorder" button that turns rows into `listbox` with `aria-grabbed` semantics or simple move-up/move-down buttons. arrow keys to navigate, Space to pick, arrows to move. announce "Row moved to position 3" in aria-live.

sam: agree on keyboard mode. simpler pattern: expose a handle button on each row with `aria-label="Move test"`. When activated, show move controls: "Move up" / "Move down" / "Done". That fits our focus model.

mara: good. microcopy: handle tooltip should read "Reorder test (keyboard friendly)". buttons: "Move up" / "Move down" -> a11y prefers verbs first so keep that order.

diego: filter chips: currently chips show label only (e.g., "regressions"). Need counts and clear state: `Regressions (4)` and a visible x to remove. When active, chip should have `aria-pressed=true` and `aria-describedby` with active-description.

jules: also add an accessible legend: "Filters applied: 3" and a "Clear all filters" button. For screenreader users, read out applied filters on change: "Filters applied: regressions, changed outputs" via aria-live.

sam: sorting: when user toggles sort from "Newest" to "Most regressions", we should announce `aria-live="polite"` message: "Sorted by most regressions; showing 12 items. Focus on first test." Then move focus to the row header.

mara: empty-state copy: current "No results" is terse. propose: "No tests match these filters. Try removing filters or run a new eval. [Run eval] [Clear filters]". Put CTAs inline and keyboard accessible.

diego: contrast: aria_bot flagged the active chip background too light. suggestion: darken to reach 3:1 contrast on chip text or add a 1px inset border.

aria_bot: accessibility-check: recommended chip active bg #E8F0FF on white yields 2.3:1 for text #1F2A44. Suggest #D0E4FF or increase text weight to 600. Also ensure chip close `x` is at least 24x24 target and has visible focus ring.

jules: another concern: when reordering large lists, we should debounce analytics and batch updates to server. UX should show a subtle saving indicator "Saving order..." and then success toast `role=status`: "Order saved". If offline, queue and show "Changes queued".

mara: analytics names: `evals.reorder.start`, `evals.reorder.move`, `evals.reorder.save`, include `moved_from`, `moved_to`, `selection_id`. keep light.

sam: keyboard shortcuts idea: `R` to toggle reorder mode, `F` to focus filter input, `Shift+F` to clear filters. Document in keyboard shortcuts modal. Show hint in UI near filters: "Press F to focus".

diego: small copy nit: when filters hide items, show a small summary: "Showing 4 of 42 tests" with a tooltip "X filtered out". helpful for context. Also allow pagination preference: infinite scroll vs pages in user prefs.

jules: implementation note: use `aria-live` politely for non-disruptive updates and `role=region` for filter summary. For reorder announcements use `aria-atomic=true` so message reads fully.

mara: action items: (mara) update mock with move handles + chip counts + empty-state CTAs (2233334450), (sam) prototype keyboard reorder controls and `aria-live` messages, (jules) add saving/queued state flows + analytics enum doc, (diego) update chip contrast and small summary copy.

mara: thanks all ":thumbsup:" will post a tiny HTML prototype in the PR for screenreader testing.\
